Had a blast playing this game! It’s fun and engaging, though there are a few minor bugs.

However, there are a few downsides. Some mechanics or features are only used once throughout the entire game, which feels like a missed opportunity. Additionally, certain cutscenes are unskippable—fine for the first playthrough, but frustrating when you want to explore different paths. Speaking of different paths, the story can feel a bit restrictive. While there are some choices to make, they often lead to the same outcome, limiting the sense of true player agency.

I rarely write a review of a game. The story line was top notch. I was very interested from playing the demo, so I had to buy it. I'm so glad I did. It had me glued to the game for almost 3 hours. Now I want to play through it again to see different outcomes. My one and only complaint, was it wasn't long enough. Highly recommended.

If you've ever wanted to be Agent 47's handler or part of X-Files' The Lone Gunmen or a member of that NSA hacker group in Enemy of The State; The Operator is kind of the closest you can get. And it's a good fantastic time: it's good, pop fun with a particularly intense sequence in the middle; and some super inspired decisions in the realization department.
It could be a bit more freeform, but hopefully a sequel will remedy to that.

It's a pretty good short game. I will say it is a bit pricey for the amount of gameplay so do add it to your wishlist so you get notified for sales. You do figure out the perp about half way through but the real twist hits you at the end. I love games like this where I go through figuring out my own little details about the cases and though there is a lot of hand holding its a good entry point into these game to go into Cyber Manhunt and Orwell!

Absolutely all around fantastic. The writing, voice acting, gameplay, soundtrack... just superbly done. I only wish it was longer, but for the price it is so worth it. Really hoping this game gets a ton of well-earned attention, because I will definitely be holding my breath for a sequel, spin-off, or really anything else from these guys. 

10/10

What a really well made and fun game. I was looking for games much like Orwell and its DLC, Ignorance is Strength, and this absolute gem of a title popped up. Great concept, fabulous story, really engaging mechanics, and an ending that I genuinely didn't expect and thoroughly enjoyed.

I finished it all in 6 hours because I'm a smoothbrain so I imagine most people will finish it in less but I promise it's well worth it.

I really hope they make some DLC so I can keep exploring this world!

This is a tough one for me to review. On the one hand, this is a very cool concept, and I think it’s executed very well. On the other, it feels very much like a proof of concept for a bigger game. 

I don’t want to get into spoilers, but I will say that I would’ve liked a few more “normal” cases to solve before jumping into the government conspiracy aspect. I feel like it would’ve made some of the later reveals stand out more. As it stands, you start the game immediately suspecting something is fishy. Your very first case kicks off the game-long mystery. 

Also, I feel like some of the reveals were done more for the immediate shock value than they were for actual plot reasons. As in, you uncover a number of secrets that feel like they don’t actually go anywhere, beyond the initial stomach-dropping “oh shit” moment. 

I would love to see this expanded upon in a sequel, which is why I’m ultimately recommending this game. The fact that my biggest complaint is that “I wanted more” should ultimately speak to the quality of the experience. Like I said, it’s got good bones. I just wish it had been fleshed out more.

I had gone into this game without reading what it was about or watching the trailer, purely recommended by someone, and I feel that made the experience a bit better for me having to actually follow along with the story as to what I would be doing next. Overall, I really enjoyed the game, and given the work that was put into it, I am not upset about the price tag for a few hours of entertainment. One thing that does disappoint, is the fact that the story is linear and that while your choices seem to change the goals, (e.g. [spoiler]the bomb diffuse going wrong[/spoiler]), it ends up the same way - but I do appreciate how the game catered to making it seem as if your choices changed the outcome.

Something that I found a bit confusing was identifying things for objectives, it sometimes was hard figuring out exactly what to identify, even when I personally knew what they were looking for. Example being a spoiler: [spoiler]I figured out early that the apartment being watched was my own, but spent a while submitting individual things like the my cat, finally realizing that I was supposed to submit my name in the top right, could 100% just be me though.[/spoiler]

I did like the game though, and am eager to follow along if updates are made to this or a new game similar were to be worked on.

I wish there was a thumbs in the middle option as down seems a little unfair. The premise The Operator and the game play itself was really interesting. I'm a big fan of detective games so I was really looking forward to what looked like a new spin on this. Unfortunately the cases themselves felt too short and like there was more focus on dialogue between the characters as opposed to me investigating or analysing evidence. The ending itself felt a little abrupt but I hope there is a sequel that expands on these story lines a little further, as I felt I was just getting to grips with the mechanics by the games end. An interesting take on a detective game

I do hope that for the time/price ratio they will not be releasing a continuation of this game as a separate game, but instead maybe an update or DLC with a lighter price.

Overall I give this game a 5/10, I would recommend it to my friends. Play it alone, in one sitting, it's a good experience.
